biggest_gap: depot.render.js:699 escapes and THEN slices: esc(str(r.assignedTo)).slice(0, 24), and the result is handed to banner(), which escapes it a second time. A contract id containing '&' renders as 'contract A&B<c>' in the player's face, and the 24-char budget is measured in escaped characters, so a 36-'&' id shows five of them and can be cut mid-entity. It is also a third length budget living outside clip(), which this revision's own header says exists so there is one. The fix is one line: clip first at a named budget, let banner() do the only escape.

builder_response: The critic was right on the substance and I confirmed it before changing anything: index.js has no slice anywhere, `S.error = String(r.why || r.error)` at line 191 is the whole treatment, and my own file's comment was claiming otherwise. I fixed it in code rather than by deleting the assertion — clip()/ERR_MAX now enforce the 160 the comment used to merely allege, and the same helper replaced the two inline .slice(0,160) calls so there is one budget instead of three. I also made truncation visible rather than silent, because an invisibly-cut message is a smaller version of the same "the panel lied about what the server said" failure. All three bundled stale claims were checked against the real files and rewritten: the two index.html citations are now 79943 and 164476/164479 (+207985), quoteForm records the defect as closed by index.js's form echo with the one limit that genuinely remains (the 15s ticker repaint eats never-submitted keystrokes), and lotBlock is documented as live with the shape index.js actually supplies. Finally I attacked the class rather than the instances: the header now states that citations lead with the symbol and that this file asserts no upstream guarantee it does not itself enforce, which is exactly the rule whose absence produced the gap.
